precepts.text: Thou leddest them in the day by a cloudy pillar, and in the night by a pillar of fire, to give them light in the way.
precepts.point: The cloud and the fire speak of spirits the Most High created, His angels: He maketh the clouds His chariot, and He maketh His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire. Fire is a spirit, created for vengeance, poured out in the time of destruction to appease the wrath of Him that made them.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Moreover thou leddest them in the day by a cloudy pillar; and in the night by a pillar of fire, to give them light in the way wherein they should go.”

Israel did not have to rely on maps. The cloud of the Lord upon the tabernacle by day and the fire on it by night were the navigation system: when the cloud was taken up they journeyed, and if it was not taken up they journeyed not until the day it was taken up. Our forefathers were blessed to witness these things firsthand, and it should be very exciting to read of the pillar and the glory our ancestors saw in the wilderness.

precepts.text: In thy manifold mercies thou forsookest them not in the wilderness; the pillar of cloud and the pillar of fire departed not from them.
precepts.point: The cloud and the fire speak of spirits the Most High created, His angels: He maketh the clouds His chariot, and He maketh His angels spirits, His ministers a flaming fire. note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Yet thou in thy manifold mercies forsookest them not in the wilderness: the pillar of the cloud departed not from them by day, to lead them in the way; neither the pillar of fire by night, to shew them light, and the way wherein they should go.”

The Most High in His manifold mercies forsook them not. The cloud was upon the tabernacle by day and the fire by night “in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys”; they had no need to create their own lamps, for the Lord gave them light freely.

“There be spirits that are created for vengeance, which in their fury lay on sore strokes; in the time of destruction they pour out their force, and appease the wrath of him that made them. Fire, and hail, and famine, and death, all these were created for vengeance”.

Fire is a spirit. It is one of the spirits created for vengeance, poured out in the time of destruction to appease the wrath of Him that made them. The fire that was on the tabernacle by night was a spirit the Most High created, as His ministers are a flaming fire.

precepts.why:
“The angel of the Lord encampeth round about them that fear him, and delivereth them.”

precepts.text: An angel went before Israel to keep them in the way; obey his voice and provoke him not, and the Lord will be an enemy unto thine enemies and cut off the nations.
precepts.point: If Israel obeyed the angel's voice, the Lord would be an enemy unto their enemies and cut off the nations of the land before them. The scripture makes a distinction: the enemy whose ox or ass you must bring back and help is your brother that hates you, as the parallel law shows by using the word brother; the enemies of the nations are those the Most High said He would cut off. So love thine enemies does not mean the nation Israel was sold to; it speaks of your brother that you may be at odds with.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“Behold, I send an Angel before thee, to keep thee in the way, and to bring thee into the place which I have prepared. Beware of him, and obey his voice, provoke him not; for he will not pardon your transgressions: for my name is in him.” The cloud by day and the fire by night that led the house of Israel in all their journeys go with this Angel sent before them.

That shows why the first generation did not make it to the promised land. They provoked the angel, transgressed, complained, worshipped idols and wanted to go back into Egypt, and he will not pardon your transgressions.

“But if thou shalt indeed obey his voice, and do all that I speak; then I will be an enemy unto thine enemies, and an adversary unto thine adversaries.” The Angel would bring them in unto the Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, “and I will cut them off.” Those are the enemies of the nations, whom the Most High said He would cut off.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“If thou meet thine enemy’s ox or his ass going astray, thou shalt surely bring it back to him again. If thou see the ass of him that hateth thee lying under his burden, and wouldest forbear to help him, thou shalt surely help with him.”

The scripture makes a distinction. This enemy, whose ox or ass you must bring back and whom you must help, is your brother that hates you. In the same chapter the Lord promises to be an enemy unto Israel's enemies and to cut off the nations of the land; those enemies are not the ones whose ox you bring back.

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not see thy brother’s ass or his ox fall down by the way, and hide thyself from them: thou shalt surely help him to lift them up again.”

This is the parallel law to Exodus 23:4-5, and it uses the word brother. The enemy whose ox or ass you bring back and help is your brother that hates you, not the nations the Most High said He would cut off before the Angel.

note.label: Exodus 40: The Tabernacle Reared Up and the Glory of the Lord

precepts.why:
“But I say unto you, Love your enemies, bless them that curse you, do good to them that hate you, and pray for them which despitefully use you, and persecute you”.

Love thine enemies does not mean the nation Israel was sold to. The law that says bring back thine enemy's ox and help him that hateth thee is the law that says thy brother's ass or his ox; the enemy is your brother that you may be at odds with. The enemies of the nations are those the Most High said He would cut off when Israel obeyed the Angel's voice, and He would be an enemy unto those enemies.

precepts.text: Aaron and his sons were anointed and sanctified to minister in the priest's office, an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.
precepts.point: Aaron was consecrated and anointed to minister in the priest's office, and his sons were clothed and anointed as their father, an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.

note.label: Leviticus 22: The Holy Things and Offerings Without Blemish

precepts.why:
The Levitical priesthood was established in Aaron and his sons. “thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments, and anoint him, and sanctify him; that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.” His sons were clothed with coats and anointed “as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister unto me in the priest’s office: for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.”

Because Aaron and his sons were sanctified for that office, certain things were consecrated that the rest of Israel could not touch, and even a priest “having his uncleanness upon him” could not go unto the holy things, lest that soul be cut off from the presence of the Most High. The anointing set them apart, and the holy things were kept apart with them.

precepts.text: When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys; Numbers revisits what Exodus recorded.
precepts.point: At the commandment of the Lord they rested in the tents, and at the commandment of the Lord they journeyed; they kept the charge of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Numbers 9: The Second Passover and the Cloud over the Tabernacle

precepts.why:
“And when the cloud was taken up from the tabernacle, then after that the children of Israel journeyed: and in the place where the cloud abode, there the children of Israel pitched their tents.” Numbers revisits what Exodus recorded: “And when the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys.”

Wherever the chariot went, Israel got up and followed it, the same way it led them across the Red Sea. Whether it were two days, or a month, or a year that the cloud tarried, they abode in their tents; and when it was taken up they journeyed, whether by day or by night. That is how they knew where they needed to stay and when to move: at the commandment of the Lord they rested, and at the commandment of the Lord they journeyed, keeping the charge of the Lord by the hand of Moses.

precepts.text: When the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle the children of Israel journeyed, and when it stayed they journeyed not, for the cloud of the Most High was upon it by day and fire by night.
precepts.point: The lesson is that the Most High wants us on one accord, moving when He moves and standing when He stands, just as the powers of heaven do only what He commands.

note.label: Ezekiel 1: The Vision by the River Chebar

precepts.why:
“And when the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward in all their journeys: But if the cloud were not taken up, then they journeyed not till the day that it was taken up. For the cloud of the Lord was upon the tabernacle by day, and fire was on it by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.”

That is the wheels of Ezekiel in the wilderness. “When those went, these went; and when those stood, these stood”: when the cloud was taken up Israel journeyed, and when it stayed they journeyed not. The spirit in the chariot is Christ; wherever He said go, the chariots went, and when He stood still, they stood still.

points: Aaron and his sons were brought to the door of the tabernacle and washed with water; before they entered they were bathed, spotless. Then they were clothed and anointed to minister in the priest's office, for their anointing shall surely be an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations. The garments, the mitre, the sanctification, and the everlasting priesthood were opened at length in the Exodus 26 through 29 session.
